newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares break 5-day bull run, to test peaks.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares break 5-day bull run, to test peaks.

text.p: ** (1230 GMT) - Indian stocks end off intra-day highs
hit by bout of local profit-taking, traders say
** Bombay index closes 25.01 pts, or 0.55 pct, at 4,523.01
lower after surging nine pct in five days
** Index likely to test record high of 4,643.31 set on
September 21, 1994, traders say
** Reuter poll of 6-mth India company results for 27 firms
in Bombay share index shows overall growth, but steel,
cement and auto firms hit hard
** National bourse index ends 19.80 pts up at 1,292.90 in
curtailed trade, Delhi down 13.38 pts at 944.17
A reaction in Indian blue chips triggered by local profit-taking derailed a five-day-old bull run, traders said.

But they said the easing in prices did not spell the end of the roaring Bombay rally that has bolstered the index 47 percent higher, making it the best performing emerging market in Asia till the first half of 1997.

"I am stil not convinced that the market's going to come down sharply," said Jaspreet Ahuja, head of sales at Caspian Research (India) in Bombay. "Even if it does it will be a correction which is good."

The Bombay index shed 25.01 points to close at 4,523.01. The index earlier charged past the 4,600 mark, hitting a 34-month high of 4,605.41 -- just shy of its all-time high of 4,643.31 set on September 12, 1994.
A Reuter poll of first half company results ending June 30, 1997 for 27 firms in the BSE index issued on Wednesday also dampened the market's mood, participants said.

Steel, cement and automobiles were hit hard in the earnings forecast but the poll showed overall growth. "The market took a hit after Reuters flashed the forecasts, but I think the market just needed an excuse," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.

The net profit of cement giant Associated Cement Companies was forecast to slide 64.7 percent, to an average 194.10 million rupees in the first half of 1997/98 (April-March) from 550.50 million in the year-ago period.
ACC shares skid 108.25 rupees, or 6.5 percent, to 1,564.0.
A decision by the National Stock Exchange to postpone new account trade to Thursday came as a dampener for the market, with operators unable to build fresh positions, dealers said.
"There may be a little correction but not much. The basic direction is still positive," said Prashant Purker, head of institutional sales at Peregrine Capital India Ltd.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
